claims.text: A liquid-precursor synthesis route followed by annealing enables complete conversion to single-phase ZrB2 at about 1800 °C.
The liquid-precursor route produces nanoscale, homogeneous mixing of the reactive zirconium and boron precursors.
Nanoscale homogeneous precursor mixing permits ZrB2 formation at a lower temperature than conventional processing.
The proposed processing route produces dense, low-porosity ZrB2.
The resulting microstructure resists hole formation during prolonged exposure to a liquid plating bath.
Liquid-precursor-derived ZrB2 has mechanical performance comparable to or better than ZrB2 conventionally sintered above 2300 °C.
Annealing at 1800–1900 °C in an inert atmosphere eliminates residual impurities.
Annealing at 1800–1900 °C ensures phase-pure ZrB2 before final densification.
The process yields homogeneously distributed nanoscale ZrB2 crystallites.
The process significantly reduces residual porosity.
Molecular-level precursor mixing reduces the diffusion distances required for ZrB2 formation.
Reduced diffusion distances accelerate the ZrB2 formation reaction at reduced temperatures.
Post-synthesis annealing heals microstructural defects in ZrB2.
A dense and structurally uniform ZrB2 product has enhanced resistance to pore formation under liquid plating conditions.
Conventionally sintered single-phase ZrB2 typically has a coarser microstructure than the proposed liquid-precursor-derived material.
Conventionally sintered single-phase ZrB2 typically has higher interconnected porosity than the proposed material.
Higher interconnected porosity increases the vulnerability of ZrB2 to structural degradation in liquid plating environments.

contradictions.description: The prediction treats mechanical strength comparable to the conventional control as a successful outcome, whereas the falsification rule requires a statistically significant improvement in mechanical strength and would therefore reject merely comparable performance.
